  - Neuromodulation fell 2.2% (US down 5.4%).
  - Interventional cardiology was flat.
  - Neuroscience grew only 3.2%.

- **Q3 guide:** Organic growth of about 5%, down from 6.5%. EPS $1.40–1.42. The reasons were tougher comparisons, the MiniMed exit (about 20 bps off organic growth) and pressure in China. **The story**
- Legend gets 50% of the economics of Carvykti, the BCMA CAR-T for multiple myeloma it partners with J&J. Nearly all of its value rides on that one drug.
- Q3 results were reported 11-10. Carvykti net trade sales were $710M, up 36% year on year (US $472M, +19%; ex-US $238M, +86%). Total revenue was $359.5M, in line with consensus. Gross margin was 58%.

- Operating cash flow was -$35.9M in Q3 and -$141.9M for nine months. Cash and time deposits were about $853M, with no long-term debt. Share count is up about 5% year on year.
- The stock fell about 16% on 11-10, its worst day ever. The cause was the CFO saying Street 2027 consensus sits "at the higher end of the scenarios" management is considering. He cited slower US earlier-line share gains and ex-US launch delays.

- The stock has been weak all year. A new CEO (Ingrid Zhang) started 9/15. The prior CEO's abrupt exit and a $226M offering earlier in the year hurt the stock. I saw no analyst actions after the 11-10 drop.
- On the positive side, the updated NCCN guidelines favor CAR-T over T-cell engagers when both are viable. Five-year CARTITUDE-2 data are strong. Carvykti reached 373 treatment sites in 20 markets, and 50% of US volume is now in second and third line.

**Suncor (SU), 7:50 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-24: research for the one-to-ten-session trade decision**

**Bottom line:** The company's results are strong. The stock is falling with crude oil and the Canadian heavy-oil discount, not because of anything Suncor did. Today's bounce was small and came on a day oil recovered. I'd treat it as an oil bet. It has no company catalyst of its own in the next few sessions, apart from possible 2027 guidance in about a month.

**The story**
- **Q3 results (reported Nov 3):** Record adjusted funds from operations of C$6.7B and free funds flow of C$5.2B. Net debt was down to C$1.75B from C$6.34B at year-end. Adjusted EPS of US$2.84 beat the US$2.25 consensus. Per the [Q3 release summary](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/suncor-energy-reports-third-quarter-223000440.html), guidance was unchanged.
- **Capital returns:** Monthly buybacks rose to C$750M from C$500M, projecting C$5.5B for 2026. The quarterly dividend rose 10% to C$0.66. Per the [earnings call transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-suncor-beats-q3-2026-estimates-shares-fall-44-93CH-5000634), the call also covered a 98% upgrader utilization rate and record refined product sales.
- **Asset sale:** Suncor is selling Terra Nova, White Rose and West White Rose to Ithaca Energy for C$1.2B upfront plus up to C$350M contingent on oil prices. These assets are about 2% of upstream output. It booked a C$1.08B non-cash impairment, and closing is expected in early 2027.
- **Guidance changes:** The 2028 production growth target was cut after the sale. The C$2B free funds flow growth target is unchanged. Full 2027 guidance is due in about a month.
- **Sell-the-news reaction:** The stock fell about 4.4% after earnings despite the beat. The call transcript attributes this to worries about the outlook, the asset sale and whether margins last. That is the article's reading, not something management said.
- **CEO change (from the search summary, not opened):** Rich Kruger becomes Executive Vice Chair in April 2027, and Peter Zebedee takes over as CEO.

**Why the stock is down 16% in 20 sessions**
- **Oil has dropped sharply.** Per [Yahoo's oil-price piece](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/why-oil-prices-falling-3-133316620.html), Brent and WTI were above $100 in October and fell more than 23% in a month. A fading war premium from the Iran conflict, Libyan supply returning and a forecast surplus of about 2 million barrels a day (IEA) are the drivers.
- **Today's oil close:** WTI settled at $82.05 (+2.3%) and Brent at $91.40. Per [The Energy Brief](https://theenergybrief94.substack.com/p/tue-recap-hormuz-strikes-lift-crude), WTI had touched $79.07 on Monday, its lowest since Aug 10, and the bounce followed projectile strikes on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. SU's 1.4% gain fits an oil bounce rather than company news.
- **The heavy-oil discount is wide.** Western Canadian Select, the Canadian heavy benchmark, traded $26.60 to $31 below WTI in November, per [Reuters via BOE Report](https://boereport.com/2026/11/12/discount-on-western-canada-select-widens-63/). That is a historically wide gap, driven by high freight rates. The latest figure I found was about $27 on Nov 16. Management called the wide discounts "non-enduring" and said Suncor is less exposed than peers.
- **Canadian oil stocks sold off together.** Per [Kalkine's coverage](https://kalkine.ca/news/energy/why-tsxcnq-tsxsu-tsximo-and-tsxcve-sank-on-the-sptsx-composite-oil-slid-to-its-lowest-close-since-late-august), Suncor fell about 4.7% on Nov 18 when WTI hit its lowest since late August.
- **Analysts:** Goldman cut its target to $70 from $78 and kept Neutral on Nov 23 (per [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-suncor-energy-nyse-su-stock-price-target-cut-by-the-goldman-sachs-group-2026-11-23/)). The consensus target is about $81. CIBC raised its Canadian-dollar target and Veritas downgraded to Reduce (search summary only). Goldman's target is still about 10% above today's close.

**What could move it over the next one to ten sessions**
- **OPEC+ meeting, Nov 29 (Sunday):** It sets 2027 production policy, and the Monday open will react to it. A cut or extended pause would help, and a surprise increase would hurt. Hormuz headlines also swing oil in both directions.
- **Iran diplomacy and shipping:** Talks look stalled, and Hormuz traffic is still about 42% below prewar levels (Kpler). A flare-up lifts oil and SU. A deal or calm adds to the supply glut.
- **Heavy-oil discount:** Narrowing helps SU and widening hurts. I found no data after Nov 16.
- **Buyback:** C$750M a month is a steady bid. At a market cap of roughly C$110B (my rough estimate), that is under 1% a month.
- **Possible 2027 guidance:** Management said about a month out, so it may fall outside this window.
- **Supreme Court climate case:** The court heard *Suncor v. Boulder County* in October. The [Stanford Law analysis](https://law.stanford.edu/2026/10/06/will-the-supreme-court-create-more-barriers-to-climate-litigation-analyzing-suncor-v-boulder-oral-arguments/) says some justices may find the case premature. I found no reported decision. A ruling is a tail risk that could land any time through June.

**Technical and trade view**

- **Risk:** Oil is still in a downtrend with a surplus forecast, and a stock this extended can keep falling if WTI breaks below $79. The after-hours price (63.78) is flat, so there is no extra signal from there.

**What HPE reported on 11-23**

I read the SEC exhibit of the earnings release and HPE's investor page for this.
- Revenue was $14.55B, up 50%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.43, against a $1.20–1.30 outlook and a Street estimate of about $1.28.

- Networking was $3.06B, up 12%. Its operating margin fell to 22.1% from 23.4%.
- Free cash flow was $1.9B for the quarter and $4.5B for the year.
- Inventory more than doubled to $14.1B from $6.4B a year earlier. Payables rose to $17.4B from $7.7B.
- The FY27 outlook was raised across the board:
  - Revenue growth of 27–35% ($59.4–63.1B), up from 13–17%.
  - Non-GAAP EPS of $5.05–5.35, up from $4.40–4.60.
  - Free cash flow of at least $5.5B, up from at least $5B.
  - Q1 revenue of $14.0–14.6B and EPS of $1.30–1.40.
- Capital return: the buyback authorization rose by $5B to about $7.3B. HPE plans to return at least 75% of FY27 free cash flow. The dividend is $0.17 a share, with a record date of 12-9.

**Why the stock fell**

These points come from Yahoo and 24/7 Wall St summaries. The two fuller articles (Invezz and Benzinga) returned 403 errors, so I couldn't open them. I didn't find a call transcript.
- **Margins:** CFO Marie Myers said costs would rise faster than prices in the second half of FY27. That would narrow gross margin even as gross profit dollars grow.
- **Cloud & AI margin:** the reported guide is about 14% for FY27, against 18.4% in Q4. Company-wide operating margin is guided to 14–15%, against 15.1% in FY26. Management had earlier pointed to a lower-margin hyperscaler deal.
- **Memory shortage:** CEO Antonio Neri expects memory, NAND and other component supply to stay tight into at least the second half of calendar 2028. HPE will keep passing costs on, but with smaller increases than before.
- **The setup going in:** the stock jumped more than 17% on 11-23 before the report and closed at $48.02, so part of today's drop is that run-up reversing. Even so, it had already lost nearly half its value from the October peak. Reasons cited were:
  - post-midterm worries about AI and data-center regulation;
  - a Barclays downgrade to Hold on 10-15;
  - Nvidia turmoil;
  - rate fears.
- **Questions on the growth quality:** networking grew only about 10% on a normalized basis. Data center networking fell 6% in the prior quarter.
- **Analyst reaction:** targets were cut but remain well above the price. Piper Sandler went to $54 from $70 (Neutral), Susquehanna to $55, Barclays to $51 and Wells Fargo to $50. These are from a search snippet, not a page I opened.
- **Valuation:** at the 11-09 price of about $45, the stock traded at about 10 times the old FY27 EPS framework. At $40 against the new $5.05–5.35, that is roughly 7.5–8 times. These are my own calculations.

- Dell had run up about 20% on Monday, and Tuesday gave most of that back. The source attributes Monday's jump to Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. That was in one article only, and I did not verify it.
- This sits inside a much bigger slide. Dell was $578 on Oct 7 and about $329 on Nov 9. Cited reasons were enterprise-AI spending timing, Barclays cutting it to Hold on Oct 14, and worry about a post-midterm crackdown on AI and data centers. Q2 free cash flow also fell 47%.

- **Q4 guide:** revenue $56.3B and non-GAAP EPS $8.40. The 8-K shows no prior figure to compare. The full-year raise implies Q4 is well above the Street's prior view.
- **Valuation:** one source puts the stock at about 10 times expected fiscal-year earnings.

**Reaction so far**
- After-hours moves vary by source, from +2% to about +5%. One had it at roughly $305, which is +3%. The sources used different reference prices, and the tape is volatile.
- The reaction is muted for a beat this large, because the sector is in a drawdown.

**What could move it over the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **Upside:**
  - A rebound in the sector if HPE's memory scare fades.
  - The new $25B buyback.
  - Analyst target raises.
  - A beat-and-raise at about 10 times earnings leaves room to fill part of the Oct–Nov drop.
- **Downside:**
  - Memory and component shortages. Both Dell and HP flagged cost pressure, and Dell expects the shortage into 2027. HPE's "through 2H 2028" comment could keep hitting margins and sentiment.
  - Balance sheet. Inventory rose to $29.4B from $10.4B in January, and debt to $37.7B from $31.5B.
  - PCs. The PC unit's revenue growth slowed to 3% from 20% last quarter, and consumer PC sales fell 15%.
  - AI-capex and political headlines, and the high volatility.
  - Fading after-hours gains. Dell's August 2025 report beat and then sold off on a soft guide.
- **To watch:** the call commentary on memory pricing and margin, and the pre-market open versus roughly $305.
